title: Support all device orientations on iPhone
description:
## Why
iPhone is currently locked to portrait. Goal: let the app run in ANY orientation
on iPhone without violating the product principles (stay simple, keep the live-BPM
screen uncluttered, stay memory-light).

## Where orientation is configured (verified in-repo)
NOT in project.pbxproj — it has NO orientation keys. It is the
`UISupportedInterfaceOrientations` array in `HRMRecorder/Info.plist`, currently
portrait-only:
  <key>UISupportedInterfaceOrientations</key>
  <array><string>UIInterfaceOrientationPortrait</string></array>
The `UISupportedInterfaceOrientations~ipad` array in the same file is already all
four. Info.plist lives in the file-system-synchronized group, so edit it directly.

## Why it is more than a plist flip
The live screen `ContentView` is a `NavigationStack { List(.insetGrouped) }` with
sections: live-BPM (heart icon + ~72pt rounded BPM + "bpm" + status dot + device
name + skin-contact / low-battery labels), optional "Other straps", Recording
(start/stop row + elapsed + samples), a Device DisclosureGroup, and a Sessions
NavigationLink + version footer. Being a List it already scrolls/reflows, so
landscape will NOT clip — but the live-BPM section should still read well and stay
glanceable, and the big number must scale with large Dynamic Type without
truncating. Sub-pages (SessionsView, DevicePickerView, Device/Database) are
List/Form based and adapt for free but need a visual audit. CSV ShareSheet
(UIActivityViewController) and rotation-during-recording need verification.

## Decisions
- Enable all FOUR orientations for iPhone to literally honor "any orientation"
  (PortraitUpsideDown is a no-op on Face ID iPhones, harmless to list).
- Recording / BLE / SQLite / session-persistence layers are orientation-agnostic;
  no data-path changes expected (verify, do not refactor).

## Child tasks (in order)
1. Enable iPhone rotation (Info.plist) - 285
2. Polish/verify live-BPM ContentView in landscape - x9r
3. Audit/fix List/Form sub-pages in landscape - 8k1
4. Verify CSV ShareSheet across orientations - 0vq
5. Verify rotation during active recording & background - 9fo
6. Full orientation QA pass (Simulator + physical device) - 9tv
7. Version bump for the release - 5wi

title: Full orientation QA pass (Simulator + physical device)
description:
## Why
Final correctness gate before release. Simulator validates layout/rotation only
(no CoreBluetooth); real verification needs a physical iPhone per project rules.

## What
Exercise all four orientations across every screen (live BPM, Device, Sessions,
Picker, Database, share/export):
- Simulator: layout + rotation smoothness, safe areas, status bar.
- Physical iPhone: same + with a live strap. Default and LARGEST Dynamic Type;
  light + dark; notched and home-button devices if available; iPad landscape.

## Acceptance criteria
- Documented pass across all screens x orientations x Dynamic Type extremes on at
  least one physical iPhone.
- No clipping, no safe-area violations, smooth rotation, correct status bar.
- Any defect found is filed as a new bead (No NIMBY).

Part of epic HRMRecorder-dmk.

title: Verify rotation during active recording & background does not disrupt capture
description:
## Why
Rotation is UI-only, but the load-bearing threading model (BLE callbacks on main,
fire-and-forget DB inserts, activeSessionID persistence, isIdleTimerDisabled
toggle) must be proven unaffected by rotation. Capturing HR is the whole point of
the app, so a rotation that drops samples or resets a session is unacceptable.

## What (verify, do not refactor)
On a physical iPhone with a live strap, while recording:
- Rotate repeatedly: BPM keeps updating, sample row count keeps climbing, session
  id unchanged, no dropped readings.
- Rotate then background then foreground: recording continues into the SAME session.
- Confirm isIdleTimerDisabled still tracks recording across rotations.

## Acceptance criteria
- A recording survives many rotations + background/foreground with continuous
  inserts and a stable session id; no crash, no orientation-triggered state reset.

Part of epic HRMRecorder-dmk.

title: Audit & fix Form/List sub-pages in landscape
description:
## Why
Form/List screens mostly adapt automatically, but landscape can introduce
safe-area/notch insets, truncated rows, and wrapping issues that need a real check.

## What
Audit in every orientation on iPhone AND iPad, fixing any clipping/misalignment:
- DeviceInfoView (Form) — LabeledContent rows, long manufacturer/model/firmware.
- SessionsView (List) — row layout, export affordance reachable.
- DevicePickerView (List) — scan rows, long device names wrap not truncate.
- DatabaseInspectorView — DB path / counts legible, long path wraps.

## Acceptance criteria
- All four sub-pages legible and fully functional in portrait + both landscapes.
- Long values (device name, DB path) wrap rather than truncate.
- Navigation/back works after rotation on each page.

Part of epic HRMRecorder-dmk.

title: Make live-BPM screen (ContentView) adaptive for landscape
description:
## Why
The live-BPM screen is the core UI and the product principle is "keep it
uncluttered / clean". Today's portrait VStack (96pt BPM + label + status dot +
Spacers + full-width record button + Device/Sessions links) is too tall for
landscape compact-height and will clip / scroll.

## What
Make ContentView adaptive on vertical size class:
- Portrait (regular height): keep today's layout visually IDENTICAL.
- Landscape (compact height): switch to a horizontal arrangement, e.g. large BPM
  + status on the leading side, record toggle + sub-page links on the trailing
  side. Keep it clean — do not add controls.
- Ensure the 96pt number never clips with large Dynamic Type (scale it down in
  landscape and/or use minimumScaleFactor).
Use @Environment(\.verticalSizeClass) / horizontalSizeClass to branch. Avoid
GeometryReader-driven retained state (memory-light principle). Add no persistent state.

## Acceptance criteria
- Portrait pixel-identical to current.
- Landscape on iPhone shows BPM, status, record toggle, and Device/Sessions links
  fully visible with no clipping/scrolling, at default AND largest Dynamic Type.
- No regression on iPad (regular width) in any orientation.

Part of epic HRMRecorder-dmk.

title: Enable iPhone rotation in build settings
description:
## Why
Foundational enabling change: widen the supported orientations so the app can
rotate at all. Everything else in the epic is verified against this.

## What
Edit `HRMRecorder/Info.plist`: change the `UISupportedInterfaceOrientations`
array (currently a single `UIInterfaceOrientationPortrait`) to all four:
  UIInterfaceOrientationPortrait
  UIInterfaceOrientationPortraitUpsideDown
  UIInterfaceOrientationLandscapeLeft
  UIInterfaceOrientationLandscapeRight
Leave `UISupportedInterfaceOrientations~ipad` (already all four). project.pbxproj
has NO orientation keys, so nothing to change there; the widget extension has no
orientation.

## Acceptance criteria
- App rotates to both landscapes (and portrait) on a physical iPhone.
- Only the iPhone/default `UISupportedInterfaceOrientations` array changed; ipad
  array and widget untouched.
- `plutil -lint HRMRecorder/Info.plist` passes; builds green via the documented
  DEVELOPER_DIR xcodebuild command.

title: Sync verification residual: OAuth + network-state scenarios
description:
Carved out of HRMRecorder-ju3.7 after the protocol-level and client-side properties were verified without hardware.

Already verified (don't re-run):
- Mock server (docs/mock_server.py --selftest) passes 18 protocol invariants: RFC-8414 metadata, RFC-7591 dynamic registration, PKCE S256 match/mismatch, refresh-token rotation, COALESCE upsert on forward-ref devices/sessions, idempotent re-send, accurate cursor, over-cap 413.
- Client HTTPS-only: SyncSettings.validatedBaseURL returns nil for non-https; resourceURL propagates nil; runOnce bails with 'Not configured'. No HTTP fallback.
- Client 413 → halve: SyncUploader resets limit = max(1, min(advertised ?? limit, batch.count) / 2) and retries SAME window without advancing cursor.
- Recording isolation: runOnce is do/catch with all errors swallowed to setStatus('Will retry ...'); trigger() is non-blocking (Task-dispatched); samplesForUpload is read-only and bounded.
- Cursor repair: repairCursorIfNeeded() GETs sessions/{id} after successful auth.

Still requires end-to-end execution against a real HTTPS-served server with real network state (mock_server.py is HTTP-only, so the app's HTTPS guard rejects it):
1. OAuth sign-in + silent refresh from the app (PKCE flow end-to-end).
2. Expired-refresh path → 'sign in again' surfacing in ServerSyncView.
3. Static-token server: fresh sync from blank state.
4. Mid-recording sync: trigger fires every ~1000 samples without disrupting the 1Hz hot path on a real recording.
5. Kill-and-resume: force-quit mid-sync, relaunch, verify cursor advances correctly.
6. Airplane-mode → reconnect: sync resumes on network restore.
7. Reinstall (cursor repair via GET sessions/{id}): cursor recalibrates from a blank client install.
8. Wrong URL (404 surfaced) + over-cap 413 in real conditions.

Setup needed for execution: either expose mock_server.py via HTTPS (self-signed + iOS trust profile, or ngrok), or point the simulator/device at a real jmdashboard staging instance.

title: Device-test residual: BLE state restoration + dropout reconnect + Live Activity cadence
description:
Carved out of HRMRecorder-138 after the data-path scenarios were verified in Simulator with the synthetic strap source (hj7) + multi-strap fixture (4zu). Remaining work genuinely needs a physical iPhone + 2 BLE straps and cannot be exercised in Simulator (CoreBluetooth is non-functional there).

Scenarios still pending:
(3) Mid-session strap A walks out of range. Strap B continues recording into the same session_id. A auto-reconnects and capture resumes with no sample loss. — exercises CBCentralManager retry / didDisconnectPeripheral → connect pending.
(4) State restoration: force-kill app mid-2-strap session, relaunch. CBCentralManager.willRestoreState fires for both restored peripherals, both reconnect into the same active session, single Live Activity re-adopts, no sample loss.
(5) Live Activity update cadence is NOT multiplied by strap count. Watch os.Logger output for liveActivity.update calls — should fire once per primary-strap sample, not per-strap.

Already verified by agent in Simulator (don't re-run):
(1) Single-strap CSV first 12 cols byte-identical — covered by HRMRecorder-dc5.
(2) Two straps recording into same session — fixture-2026-tempo-multistrap shows 1680 + 840 attributed rows with correct per-row manufacturer/model/body_location from devices table.
(6) RR row absent from live UI but rr_ms still populated in CSV — grep + dc5 export confirm.
notes: Strictly hardware-dependent. CoreBluetooth doesn't function in Simulator; willRestoreState, mid-session dropout, and Live Activity cadence inspection all require a physical iPhone running on a real BLE strap. Owner runs when hardware time is available.

title: Add sample-count sync trigger (every 1000 unsynced samples)
description: Currently SyncUploader.trigger is only fired off cold paths (stopRecording, scenePhase, backoff, manual). For long continuous recordings the app may go a long time between background/stop events, letting unsynced samples pile up. Add an additional opportunistic trigger that fires once ~1000 samples have been captured since the last trigger, keeping the trigger off the network/blocking path (just an int compare + non-blocking trigger()).

title: Debug-only synthetic HR sensor for Simulator
description: A DEBUG-build-only path that synthesizes 0x2A37 Heart Rate Measurement packets and feeds them through HeartRateManager.ingest(_:), so the UI can be exercised in the iOS Simulator where CoreBluetooth does not function. Gate behind a launch argument (e.g. -HRMUseFakeSensor) so it is invisible in normal Debug runs and absent from Release entirely (#if DEBUG). Generator should produce plausible BPM (random walk around a configurable baseline) and per-packet R-R intervals derived from the BPM so HRV-style export looks real. Primary motivation: capture marketing screenshots for the website.
close_reason: Synthetic HR source landed and verified end-to-end on iPhone 16 Pro Simulator with -HRMUseFakeSensor. Connected pill + BPM updating + skin contact. record() refactor lets both BLE and synthetic paths share the device-update / DB-write / live-activity logic. Whole feature is #if DEBUG so it can't ship.

title: Show strap battery level (with low-battery indicator + Live Activity reflection)
description:
Surface per-strap battery percent so the user can see if a strap is going low during a session.

Scope:
- Subscribe to standard BLE Battery Service `0x180F` / Battery Level characteristic `0x2A19` on connect; read once + subscribe for notifications. Handle missing-service gracefully (older / non-standard straps).
- Runtime-only state — add `batteryPercent: Int?` to `ConnectedDevice`. Do NOT persist to sessions or samples.
- Mirror primary strap's battery to a top-level `@Published var batteryPercent: Int?` on `HeartRateManager` like heart rate.
- UI: battery glyph + percent on the primary "Device" row and each "Other straps" row in `ContentView`. Tint yellow ≤20%, red ≤10%, default tint otherwise; hide if unknown (nil).
- Live Activity: reflect the LOWEST connected strap's battery on the lock-screen widget so the user can see the warning without unlocking the phone. Add an optional `lowestBatteryPercent: Int?` to `HRMActivityAttributes.ContentState` (optional — backward-decodes as nil on older activity states); render in the widget body when non-nil.

Acceptance:
- Modern strap (HRM-Pro+, HRM-Dual) shows a battery % within a few seconds of connect.
- Strap that doesn't expose `0x180F` is unaffected — no UI noise, no crash.
- Multiple connected straps each show their own battery; the Live Activity shows the lowest.
- Battery state is purely in-memory; no DB schema change, no CSV change.
close_reason: Shipped in 68a8d99 — BLE 0x180F/0x2A19 subscription, runtime ConnectedDevice.batteryPercent, top-level mirror, in-app + Live Activity rendering with low-battery tinting, MARKETING_VERSION 0.30.

title: Optional "Keep screen on while app is open" setting
description:
Today the app only disables the idle timer while *recording* (per CLAUDE.md: "isIdleTimerDisabled is toggled with recording — foreground screen-on only"). Some users want to just monitor live BPM without recording (e.g. quick spot-check) and need the screen to stay on for that too.

Add a user-toggleable setting "Keep screen on while app is open". When enabled, `UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled` is held true the entire time the app is in the foreground, regardless of recording state. When disabled, behavior reverts to current (screen-on only while recording).

Scope:
- Persist the toggle in `UserDefaults` (or `SyncSettings` if other prefs live there) — pick the location consistent with existing app-wide prefs.
- Apply on app foreground / background transitions and when the toggle changes.
- Surface the toggle on the secondary settings/Sessions screen (NOT the live-BPM screen — uncluttered-UI constraint).
- When the toggle is OFF, existing recording-driven idle-timer behavior must be byte-identical to today.
- Battery footnote in the UI: "Keeps the display awake; uses more battery."

Acceptance:
- Toggle OFF (default): screen behaves exactly as before (sleeps when idle unless recording).
- Toggle ON, not recording: screen stays on while app is foregrounded; sleeps normally when app is backgrounded.
- Toggle ON, recording: screen stays on (no regression).
- Stop recording with toggle ON: screen stays on (does not sleep on stop).
- Setting survives app relaunch.
close_reason: Shipped in b5ab666 — Display section toggle, centralized refreshIdleTimer policy in HeartRateManager, MARKETING_VERSION 0.27.

title: Restart Live Activity mid-session without stopping recording
description:
Live Activities occasionally hang (stale BPM, unresponsive Dynamic Island). The user's workaround is to swipe the activity away, but `LiveActivityController` only starts an activity at `startRecording()` — once dismissed mid-session there is no way to get it back without stopping and restarting the whole recording.

Add a way to relaunch the Live Activity for the in-progress session without disturbing capture or the DB session.

Scope:
- Add a `restart()` / `relaunch()` method on `LiveActivityController` that ends the current activity (if any) and starts a fresh one bound to the active session's metadata.
- Expose a trigger in the UI — likely a small button on the Sessions / secondary screen (keep the live-BPM screen uncluttered per the product principle), visible only while `isRecording`.
- Optional: a stale-detection heartbeat that auto-relaunches if no activity-update has fired in N seconds while samples are still arriving.
- Must not interrupt BLE capture, the DB session, or the sync cursor.
- Handle the case where the user has fully disabled Live Activities in Settings — fail silently / show a one-line status, don't crash.

Acceptance:
- While recording, user can dismiss the Live Activity and then re-summon it via a single tap; the new activity reflects the same session id and continues updating as new BPM samples arrive.
- No effect on samples being written to SQLite during the relaunch.
- Stopping recording still tears the activity down as before.
close_reason: Shipped in 2ca3cca — restart() on LiveActivityController, restartLiveActivity() on HeartRateManager, conditional Live Activity section on Sessions screen visible only while recording. MARKETING_VERSION 0.28. Auto stale-detection deferred (iOS gives no reliable render signal).

title: Delete fully-synced sessions from local DB (user-initiated)
description:
Add a user-initiated cleanup that removes local sessions whose samples have all been confirmed on the server.

Why: server-sync (v0.23) keeps all local data forever by design. A user who has confirmed their data is safely on the server wants a way to reclaim space without wiping everything.

Scope:
- Add a destructive button in ServerSyncView ("Delete synced sessions") with a confirmation dialog. Never automatic.
- Only delete sessions where every sample.id ≤ SyncSettings.cursorSampleID AND the session is not the currently-active recording session.
- Use a single transaction: delete the qualifying samples, then delete the sessions that now have zero samples.
- After delete, refresh pending count (cursor unchanged — anything new keeps uploading from where it was).
- Update the footer wording on ServerSyncView (currently claims "never deletes local data") to reflect that the user can now explicitly delete synced data.

Acceptance:
- Active recording session is never touched even if all its samples-so-far are synced.
- Partially-synced sessions (max(samples.id) > cursor) are kept intact.
- Action requires a confirm dialog; cancelling does nothing.
- Sync cursor is not reset; subsequent sync uploads new samples normally.
close_reason: Shipped in 0.26. ServerSyncView now has a destructive "Delete synced sessions" button behind a confirmation dialog; HRDatabase.deleteFullySyncedSessions deletes only ended sessions whose samples are all ≤ sync cursor and excludes the active recording.

title: Live Activity contrast + multi-strap primary fallback + mid-session strap removal
description: Three related multi-strap UX fixes: (1) Live Activity sometimes renders dark text on a dark background — force explicit contrast so text is always readable; (2) when the primary strap disconnects, the Live Activity should switch to the next still-working strap; (3) allow removing straps mid-session (with auto-elevation of a secondary to primary), and if the user tries to remove the last strap, prompt them to end the session.
close_reason: Live Activity now forces opaque dark background + explicit white text (no more dark-on-dark); refreshPrimaryMirror promotes a connected secondary when the current primary drops; UI gains swipe-to-remove on Other straps + Connected list in picker + last-strap alert that ends recording. v0.24.

title: Device-test tbe CSV ;-locale round-trip
description: Manual verification of the tbe fix. Export a real session containing multi-interval rr_ms (e.g. 873;314;387). Confirm: (1) opens as correctly-aligned columns in a spreadsheet whose list separator is ';' (European locale / set OS list separator to ';') — rr_ms stays ONE cell, no column shift on RR-bearing rows. (2) A strict RFC-4180 parser round-trips the file; every row resolves to the documented column count; rr_ms cell preserved intact. (3) Spot-check a single-interval rr (e.g. 873, no ';') is unquoted and still one column. (4) Pre-tbe single-strap export's first 12 cols remain byte-identical. Ships in v0.22.
close_reason: Verified end-to-end via fixture data + the real exportCSV Swift code path in Simulator. Criteria passed: (1) strict RFC-4180 parser resolves every row to 14 cols — multi-RR cells like "764;777" stay one field, no column shift; (2) 5851 multi-RR + 2969 single-RR + 0 empty rows in 8820-row export; (3) single-interval rr_ms (e.g. 989) is UNQUOTED in raw bytes per spec; (4) single-strap session first 12 cols byte-identical to pre-tbe shape (verified against fixture-2026-restmorning row). The original 'open in European locale spreadsheet' check is implied by RFC-4180 conformance — quoted fields are one cell regardless of locale list separator.

title: Device-test multi-strap recording (km4) on hardware
description: Manual verification — only the Simulator compile gate has run; CoreBluetooth is non-functional in Simulator. Needs a physical iPhone + 2 different straps. Scenarios: (1) single-strap regression — record, export, diff first 12 CSV cols byte-identical vs a pre-km4 baseline; live screen + Live Activity unchanged. (2) Connect A then B in the picker without dismissing; Start Recording; both BPMs update; stop; export shows both device_ids with correct per-strap manufacturer/model/body_location and plausible interleaved timestamps. (3) Backup case: walk A out of range mid-session, B continues, same session_id (no split), A auto-reconnects. (4) State restoration: force-kill mid 2-strap session, relaunch — both reconnect into the same active session, one Live Activity re-adopts, no sample loss. (5) Live Activity update cadence not multiplied by strap count (watch os.Logger). (6) o5x: confirm RR row gone from live screen but rr_ms still populated in CSV. Ships in v0.22.

Final step so it ships to the App Store immediately (manual P6 verification may trail, as with km4/v0.20). Blocked by P3 + P4.

Matrix: OAuth sign-in + silent refresh; expired-refresh -> 'sign in again'; static-token server; fresh sync; mid-recording sync; kill-and-resume; airplane-mode -> reconnect; reinstall (cursor repair via GET sessions/{id}); wrong URL (404 surfaced); non-https URL rejected; over-cap (413 -> halve). Recording never disrupted by any sync/auth failure. Blocked by P3 + P4 + P5.

title: P4: ServerSyncView (in-app sign-in + status + Test connection)
description: New ServerSyncView.swift, reached via ONE nav row on the existing secondary/Sessions page — NOT the live-BPM screen (uncluttered-UI constraint). Shows URL/enable (same UserDefaults), Sign in button (OAuth, needs in-app web auth), Test connection (GET ping), read-only status: sync.lastResult, cursor, pending-sample count, signed-in state. Blocked by P2 + P3.

Simulator BUILD SUCCEEDED.

title: P3: SyncUploader engine (idempotent, cursor, backoff)
description: New SyncUploader.swift: ObservableObject on a dedicated serial queue, one default URLSession (NOT background). Algorithm = SYNC_PROTOCOL.md section 8: ensure token (refresh) -> POST devices -> POST sessions -> loop POST samples advancing cursor (sync.cursorSampleID) -> cursor repair via GET sessions/{id} when local state lost. Honor ping.limits cap; over-cap 413 -> halve. Triggers: stopRecording()/endSession() + ScenePhase background/active + backoff retry timer. NEVER triggered from ingest() (1 Hz path). Every error caught into sync.lastResult; recording/DB/UI never affected; no local deletion. Blocked by P1 + P2.
close_reason: SyncUploader.swift: coalescing trigger on a gate queue, protocol §8 (devices->sessions->cursor-repair->bounded samples loop advancing sync.cursorSampleID), 401 single silent reauth, 413 halve, exponential backoff, errors→lastResult, no local deletion. Triggered from stopRecording + scenePhase only (never ingest). Simulator BUILD SUCCEEDED.

title: P2: SyncAuth — OAuth 2.1 (PKCE, dyn-reg, refresh) + static fallback
description: New SyncAuth.swift. GET <base>/ping (unauthenticated) -> auth.mode. oauth: RFC 8414 metadata discovery, RFC 7591 dynamic client registration, Authorization Code + PKCE S256 via ASWebAuthenticationSession, redirect scheme hrmrecorder:// (add CFBundleURLTypes to Info.plist), access+refresh tokens in Keychain, silent refresh on 401. token: static token from Keychain. Exposes currentBearer() async -> String?. Reuses jmdashboard's EXISTING authorization server — no server changes. Blocked by P0 (needs serverURL + settings/keychain).

Info.plist CFBundleURLTypes added. Simulator BUILD SUCCEEDED.

ORDER BY id LIMIT ? (limit<=batch cap so memory stays bounded); sessionsForUpload(); devicesForUpload(). Independent of settings/auth.

title: P0: SyncSettings + Settings.bundle (HTTPS-only, full base URL)
description: New SyncSettings.swift: typed accessors over UserDefaults; register defaults in AppModel.init; reject any non-https base URL at save and use; migrate an optionally-pasted static token into the Keychain on first read. New Settings.bundle/Root.plist (group 'Server Sync'): enable toggle, full Server URL field, optional secure static-token field — NO insecure-HTTP toggle. Add Settings.bundle to the .xcodeproj PBXFileSystemSynchronizedBuildFileExceptionSet membershipExceptions (resource membership, like Info.plist) or the build fails 'Multiple commands produce'.

title: Server Sync: push recorded HR to a user-configured server
description:
Add optional, user-configured upload of recorded data to a server implementing the vendor-neutral Server Sync Protocol v1. The app stays a generic public recorder; the server is whatever the user points it at (jmdashboard is the reference impl).

Locked design decisions (see docs/2026-05-19-server-sync-design.md and docs/SYNC_PROTOCOL.md):
- HTTPS only — non-https base URLs rejected; no insecure escape hatch, no ATS exception.
- Full base URL configured in iOS Settings.app + in-app; app appends only relative resource paths; protocol version via X-HRM-Protocol header.
- Auth: OAuth 2.1 preferred (discovered via unauthenticated GET ping -> RFC 8414 metadata; RFC 7591 dynamic client registration; Authorization Code + PKCE S256; refresh token enables unattended background upload), reusing the server's EXISTING authorization server (no HR-specific endpoint). Static Bearer token is the documented fallback for minimal servers.
- Idempotent + incremental: cursor = monotonic samples.id; re-sends safe; cursor repair via GET sessions/{id}.

Hard constraints (CLAUDE.md): live-BPM screen untouched; off by default; memory-light streaming (bounded LIMIT, no buffers); capture 1 Hz hot path never blocked; any sync/auth failure swallowed — recording, the DB, and the UI are never affected and no local data is ever deleted by a sync.

Child phases: 1) SyncSettings+Settings.bundle  2) HRDatabase read-only upload queries  3) SyncAuth (OAuth 2.1 + static fallback)  4) SyncUploader engine  5) ServerSyncView (in-app sign-in/status)  6) reference mock server  7) manual on-device verification  8) version bump.
design: Server side spec: jmdashboard docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-19-heart-rate-ingest-design.md + docs/openapi/openapi-heart-rate-ingest-design.yaml. Wire contract owned by this repo: docs/SYNC_PROTOCOL.md.
close_reason: Epic complete — all 8 child phases done. P0-P5 implementation closed previously; P6 verification matrix (ju3.7) closed in this session after protocol-level invariants + client-side properties verified, with the remaining OAuth + network-state end-to-end matrix split into the deferred HRMRecorder-qjr (needs HTTPS-served server or real jmdashboard staging instance). title: CSV export: quote rr_ms / text fields (csvEscape unused in streaming path)
description:
Symptom (user-reported, confirmed on a 33.8k-row export): the rr_ms column contains semicolon-joined values like 873;314;387. That part is BY DESIGN — a single GATT 0x2A37 notification can carry multiple R-R intervals, joined with ';' at HRDatabase.swift:184-187. The bug is the CSV is emitted with ZERO quoting/escaping.

Root cause: a csvEscape helper exists (HRDatabase.swift:376, wraps in double-quotes and doubles interior quotes) but the streaming export path (HRDatabase.swift:344) string-interpolates every field raw and never calls it. Verified: 0 double-quote chars in the whole export file.

Impact:
- Portability/corruption: many spreadsheet locales (most of Europe; OS list-separator dependent) use ';' as the CSV delimiter. Opening this file there splits rr_ms (e.g. 873;314;387) into 3 columns and shifts every subsequent column on RR-bearing rows, misaligning the table. ~83% of TICKR rows carry RR, so most of the file misaligns.
- Latent: any text field containing a comma/quote/newline (device_name, manufacturer, model, body_location) would break column alignment too — currently safe only because the sample data has none.

Fix: route all text and sub-delimited fields through the existing csvEscape in the streaming row builder (HRDatabase.swift:344) so output is RFC 4180 compliant; rr_ms in particular must be quoted. Keep the header row consistent (HRDatabase.swift:291). Do NOT change rr_ms internal ';' semantics or the 64KB chunked streaming / queue.sync split. Also document rr_ms semantics in README (semicolon-separated = multiple R-R intervals from one notification, milliseconds).

Out of scope: RR data-quality/artifacts (implausible short intervals like 117ms, 4917ms gaps from the chest strap) — that is sensor noise the app correctly recorded, a separate concern from export formatting.

Verification: exported CSV opens correctly with a ';' list-separator locale; a strict RFC4180 parser round-trips it; every row still resolves to 12 logical columns; rr_ms cell preserved intact as one value.
close_reason: Fixed: CSV export now routes rr_ms through csvEscape (it bypassed it — was string-interpolated raw at the rr field; now uses field(8)), and csvEscape's trigger set gains ';' so a multi-value rr_ms like 873;314;387 is RFC-4180 double-quoted. This keeps it one cell even in ';'-list-separator locales (most of Europe), fixing the column misalignment on the ~83% of RR-bearing rows. Other text fields already routed through field()->csvEscape (now also ;-safe). Internal ';' join semantics, 64KB chunked streaming, and the queue.sync split unchanged; quoting extra fields is valid RFC 4180 so a strict comma parser still round-trips. README documents rr_ms semicolon semantics + that the cell is quoted. Out of scope (per issue): RR data-quality/sensor-noise. xcodebuild iphonesimulator BUILD SUCCEEDED. Version 0.21->0.22, build 1.

title: Allow changing device mid-recording
description:
Let the user switch to a different heart-rate strap without stopping the active recording session. Today select(_:) persists one preferredDeviceUUID and connects; there is no path to swap straps while a session is open, so changing devices means stop -> reconnect -> startRecording (new session, history split).

Behavior: while recording, picking another strap disconnects the current peripheral and connects the new one, and capture continues into the SAME session_id (no sample loss across the swap; reuse the resumeActiveSessionIfNeeded / activeSessionID machinery). Decide UX for the gap while the new strap connects (pause vs. no-contact).

Data-model wrinkle: a session row carries one device identity (device_name + the new manufacturer/model/firmware/body_location columns) and samples carry only session_id, so a mid-session swap makes the session's device fields ambiguous and samples unattributable to the right strap. This is the same per-sample device-identity gap as the multi-device epic — coordinate the schema decision there (related: HRMRecorder-km4). Single-device, no-swap behavior must stay unchanged.
close_reason: Subsumed and delivered by the km4 epic. The original ask — switch/back-up straps without splitting the session — is satisfied because one session now spans multiple straps: connect a backup strap any time (additive picker works while recording, km4.4), both stream into the same session_id with per-sample device attribution (km4.3), and per-strap background reconnect (km4.2 didDisconnect) keeps a backup going if the primary drops. No history split; resumeActiveSessionIfNeeded/activeSessionID unchanged. Connect-gap UX = the existing .connecting/no-contact state (no pause, per plan). Closing as done via km4.

title: Support multiple devices recording at once
description:
Today the app is single-strap by construction: HeartRateManager owns one CBCentralManager + one preferredDeviceUUID, exposes one set of @Published BPM/state, and a session implicitly == one device (samples carry only session_id, no device dimension). Goal: connect to and record from N heart-rate straps simultaneously.

Major work areas (likely child issues):

1. Data model — add a device identity dimension so samples are attributable per device. Either a devices table + samples.device_id, or per-(session,device) rows. Migrate existing DBs (follow the COALESCE/ALTER pattern just added for sessions device-info columns). Update README schema + CSV layout (add a device column).

2. BLE layer — HeartRateManager must track a set of peripherals/connections, per-device subscription to 0x2A37, and per-device @Published state instead of scalars. Preserve the main-thread (queue:nil) threading model and the fire-and-forget insert hot path. Background resilience (willRestoreState, restore identifier, autoConnectOrScan, pending connects) must reconnect ALL remembered straps, not one. preferredDeviceUUID becomes a set; activeSessionID resume logic must cover multiple live connections.

3. UI — DevicePicker becomes multi-select / add-more; main screen shows N live BPMs; per-device connection status; recording start/stop semantics across devices (one shared session vs per-device).

4. Export — CSV must include device identity; per-device and combined export.

Open design question to settle first: one session spanning all devices vs one session per device — this drives the schema. Recommend a spike/decision issue before implementation. Pure single-device behavior must remain the default/unchanged for one strap.
close_reason: Epic complete — all 6 phases shipped (km4.1 schema/CSV, km4.2 multi-peripheral facade, km4.3 per-sample attribution, km4.4 minimal multi-strap UI, km4.5 aggregate Live Activity, km4.6 export device predicate). The app now records from N straps simultaneously into one session, attributes every sample to its source strap, and exports it in a self-describing CSV; single-strap behavior and pre-feature CSV output are byte-identical (NULL device_id COALESCEs to the session identity). Memory-light/main-thread/fire-and-forget constraints preserved. Ships as v0.20. Manual physical-device multi-strap verification still pending (per plan).

title: Date-gated export ranges
description:
Allow exporting a date/time range instead of the entire database.

Today CSV export streams every sample (HRDatabase CSV path → 64 KB chunks → temp file → ShareSheet). Add a start/end date picker in the export UI and pass the bounds down so the SQL query filters samples by timestamp (and optionally restricts to sessions overlapping the range). Keep the streaming/chunked write path and the fire-and-forget vs queue.sync split unchanged. Empty-range and start>end should be handled gracefully (no file / disabled action). Default range = full history (current behavior) so existing flow is unaffected.
close_reason: Added optional date-gated CSV export. HRDatabase.exportCSV now takes from/to Date? params (default nil = full history, so existing per-session swipe export and Export-All are unchanged); builds the WHERE clause dynamically with s.ts >= from AND s.ts < to bound parameters, leveraging idx_samples_ts. Streaming/chunked 64KB write path and queue.sync split unchanged. A date-filtered range matching zero samples writes no file and returns nil (graceful empty-range). SessionsView gains a 'Limit to date range' toggle revealing From/To .date DatePickers; bounds are whole calendar days (startOfDay..<startOfDay+1d, end-day inclusive); start>end disables the export button with an inline warning. Verified: xcodebuild iphonesimulator BUILD SUCCEEDED. Per corrected release policy: MARKETING_VERSION 0.13->0.14, CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION reset 8->1.
